label: Sumerian (transliteration)
notes: The Sumerian is the opening of the poem Gilgamesh, Enkidu and the Netherworld, lines 1-26, as the Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature gives it in its composite text, pieced together from tablets from Nippur, Ur and elsewhere. Its first line, "ud re-a ud su₃-ra₂ re-a", is the opening Peter Pringle sings.

Sign values carry their index numbers (su₃, ra₂), and a sign written before a word to say what kind of thing it is stands in braces: {d} before a god's name, {ĝiš} before things of wood. ETCSL's spelling is set in the usual signs (š, ĝ, ḫ); the words are unchanged.

The English is ETCSL's translation, which renders lines 1-26 as one passage; it is set here in lines at its semicolons and full stops. A question mark in brackets is ETCSL's own, where the meaning is uncertain.
